Contacts_x0020_Inputlog.Notes:
Returned: csab3738@uibk.ac.atMy thesis is about knowledge and writing (my promoter is Hanspeter Ortner, Institute of German Language, Literature and Literary Criticism; University of Innsbruck). I'm especially interested in academic writing of students. I want to try to find out which strategies students use to transform the knowledge they get from scientific texts to write their own texts (papers). Therefore I'm going to try to observe the writing procedure of some students from the very first moment they get into contact with the topic of their text until they hand the text in. I know that actually it's impossible to observe that but I will try to get some kind of "snapshots" of their writing procedures.
To observe the reading process I will ask them to think aloud while reading a text which serves them as a source for their own text. I'm going to record the students with two video cameras so that it's possible to see simultaneously the upper part of the reader's body and what he is doing with the text (highlighting etc.).
My theory is that a lot of writing problems (in the area of scientific or academic writing) are hidden comprehension problems. I hope that if I compare the logging or revision protocols (pause analysis etc.) of the texts
the students write with the results of the reading analysis it will be possible to see if there is a connection between the problems of comprehension and the problems of writing.

Contacts_x0020_Inputlog.Name: Marion Tillema
Contacts_x0020_Inputlog.Notes: Ik ga onderzoek doen naar de invloed van veranderende taakomstandigheden (vooral de invloed van een T2-taak) op de standaardistributie van cognitieve processen (plannen, structureren, formuleren, reviseren etc.). Het idee is dat er bepaalde patronen van processen zijn die het meest effectief zijn gebleken in T1 (bv. - even kort door de bocht - plannen moet je vooral aan het begin van het schrijfproces doen, als je een kwalitatief goede tekst wilt schrijven). Veranderende taakomstandigheden kunnen een verstoring van het standaardpatroon voor elk cognitief proces opleveren (door cognitieve overload wordt er niet meer op het juiste moment gepland), waardoor de tekstkwaliteit zal verminderen. Bovendien kan het ook nog eens zo zijn dat het meest effectieve patroon er voor verschillende taken/talen anders uit kan zien. Het gaat dus om onderzoek naar het verloop van het schrijfproces. Tot nu toe werd hiervoor voornamelijk de hardopdenkmethode gebruikt. Aangezien het voor mijn onderzoek echter erg belangrijk is om de tijdstippen waarop iets gedaan wordt nauwkeurig te registreren, is het misschien een optie om Inputlog te gebruiken naast de hardopdenkmethode.

my name is Christiane Hör and I'm working on a research2 project about autism and facilitated communication at the university of education in Heidelberg, Germany. For our project I would like to use "inputlog" for keystroke logging and to request the password. Following there's a short description of our research2 project:
With "Facilitated Communication" (FC) especially people with autism are touched at their hands or other bodily parts and can produce sophisticated texts. Therefore a variety of children and adolescents with autism were able to change from the school for mentally retarded to a general school. But until today there is still a lack of understanding about the question how and why FC is actually working. Our objective is to acquire expertise about the effect of FC, the role of the facilitator's influence and the interaction of facilitator and client. In a series of several single case studies we want to analyse errors and reaction times via keystroke logging and via video recordings whether facilitation influences the content of the text or the organisation of the writing action in an effective way. For this reason we are going to log the writing and film the writing process from several angles and compare the different perspectives simultaneously frame by frame on one screen.
With best wishes,
Christiane Hör

Contacts_x0020_Inputlog.Notes: Research2: Allow me to introduce myself: my name is Anna Katharina Schnell and I have just started my doctoral dissertation with Prof. Dr. Krings at University Bremen. At its focus it has the analysis of writing processes of foreign language learners. It is planned to observe 30 German university students of French with regard to their development of writing skills. The main tools used for our research2 will be ‘think-aloud protocols’, retrospective questionings about writing processes (control group), two questionnaires about writing and learning strategies, class observations and interviews with individuals concerning their writing biographies. As you are an acknowledged expert in the field of writing research2 who has examined long term production contexts, I would like to ask you if you have ever used a program like this or if you know anybody who owns such software. I am very much interested in purchasing such a ‘writing processing documentation program’.
